entry.name: Market thesis review
entry.summary: A bull-versus-bear research panel on one ticker: four analysts, a debate, a risk rotation, a human sign-off, a journal that scores the call.
entry.description:
Runs a small research firm over a single ticker and leaves behind an argument you can audit rather than a number you have to trust.
Four specialist analysts — technical, sentiment, news & macro, and fundamentals — work from the same verified price snapshot, each stating a stance and, more usefully, what would have to be true for it to be wrong. Each analyst is its own step holding ONLY its own tools, and each sits behind a route, so choosing a subset of the panel skips the rest through the engine rather than through an agent's good behaviour.
A bull and a bear then debate under a round budget, engaging each other's last answer instead of restating openings, and every round is frozen to its own file so the history is readable afterwards. A research manager picks a side and writes the investment plan; a trader turns it into a concrete proposal; three risk officers — aggressive, conservative and neutral — argue it in rotation under a second budget. A portfolio manager issues the final decision, and a human signs THAT step before the run may complete. The approval can be given outside the terminal, from a browser or a webhook, without the run losing its place.
The decision is appended to a journal that a later run scores against realized return and alpha versus a benchmark, then reflects on — so the panel starts each analysis having read how its previous calls actually did, on this ticker and on others.
Every handoff between steps is checked against a schema before the next step may start, so a malformed analyst report or an out-of-vocabulary recommendation stops the run rather than propagating. No subagent step has a shell: every one of the fourteen declares `deny: [shell]`, so an analyst reaches its data through the declared tools or not at all — it cannot write its own fetcher, and it cannot invoke a bundled script behind the tool layer's back. (Enforced by the generated per-step agent definition on hosts that have one; instruction-only on Cursor and Codex, which have no per-step identity.)
Per run you choose the analyst subset, the two round budgets, the report language (which the sign-off question also speaks), stock or crypto, and the data vendor. There is no LLM API key: the harness you already run supplies the model, and the default vendor is keyless — an optional Alpha Vantage or FRED key only widens the data, and without one the affected tools report the gap honestly instead of inventing numbers. Nothing is written outside the run directory and the decision journal.
A behavioral-parity reconstruction of TauricResearch/TradingAgents (Apache-2.0): the agent roles with their tasks (prompts carried over nearly verbatim), the process logic, the tool vocabulary and the decision memory are theirs; the execution machinery is Riglane's. The source repository is MIT with that Apache-2.0 carve-out — its NOTICE and the TradingAgents license travel with the code.
NOT INVESTMENT ADVICE. This produces a written argument and a recorded decision for research and workflow-demonstration purposes only.

script_tools:
  - name: write_run_config
    description: |
      The whole configure step as one deterministic call: resolves the instrument identity (shared with resolve_instrument), the analysis date (today when empty), the analyst subset, the language note, and writes the schema-validated data/run-config.json. Keyless, one identity lookup.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/write-run-config.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/write-run-config.mjs
  - name: render_report
    description: |
      Renders a role's Markdown report from its JSON artifact — the exact shapes their render_* functions produce. Write the JSON output first, then call this; the md cannot diverge from the json by construction. kind trader reads data/trader-proposal.json; research_manager reads data/research-plan.json; portfolio_manager reads data/final-decision.json.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/render-report.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/render-report.mjs
  - name: record_decision
    description: |
      Memory phase A as code (their store_decision): appends the approved decision to .user/market-thesis/decisions.jsonl as a pending entry plus the human mirror in decisions.md. Idempotent — an existing pending entry for the same (date, ticker) is reported, never duplicated. No arguments; reads the run's own artifacts.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/record-decision.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/record-decision.mjs
  - name: assemble_report
    description: |
      Their save_reports as code: copies every existing section into data/report/ (1_analysts .. 5_portfolio) and writes complete_report.md with the exact heading structure. Skips sections whose source does not exist (a deselected analyst leaves no report). No arguments.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/assemble-report.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/assemble-report.mjs
  - name: build_past_context
    description: |
      Their get_past_context as code: writes data/past-context.md from the decision journal — up to 5 resolved same-ticker entries plus 3 cross-ticker lessons, or the exact sentence "No past decisions recorded yet." The judgement half of memory (reflections) stays with the agent.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/build-past-context.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/build-past-context.mjs
  - name: resolve_instrument
    description: |
      Deterministic identity for a ticker: company name, sector, industry, exchange, quote type — plus a ready-made instrument_context sentence that anchors every agent to the REAL company instead of pattern-matching the price chart to a wrong one. Fail-open: when the source cannot resolve the symbol it returns a ticker-only context, never an error. Keyless, reads only.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/resolve-instrument.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/resolve-instrument.mjs
  - name: resolve_outcomes
    description: |
      Memory phase B, the mechanical part: reads the decision journal (.user/market-thesis/decisions.jsonl), finds this ticker's pending entries, computes each one's realized 5-day raw return AND alpha against the ticker's regional benchmark (suffix map: .T -> ^N225, .HK -> ^HSI, ..., default SPY), writes the figures back into the journal, and returns the entries that now need a written reflection. An entry whose price data is not available yet (too recent) stays pending — that is normal, not an error. Keyless, writes only the journal.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/resolve-outcomes.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/resolve-outcomes.mjs
  - name: get_stock_data
    description: |
      OHLCV price rows for a ticker, as a formatted table. Say the window the easy way — curr_date plus look_back_days — the way get_indicators does; an explicit start_date/end_date pair is accepted when you truly mean specific endpoints. Retrieve the price series FIRST — get_indicators computes from it. Keyless (Yahoo), reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-stock-data.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-stock-data.mjs
  - name: get_indicators
    description: |
      ONE technical indicator for a ticker, computed over a look-back window and reported per day. Exact indicator names: close_50_sma, close_200_sma, close_10_ema, macd, macds, macdh, rsi, boll, boll_ub, boll_lb, atr, vwma. Call once per indicator. The values are computed — read them, never recompute. Keyless (computed from Yahoo prices), reads only.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-indicators.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-indicators.mjs
  - name: get_verified_snapshot
    description: |
      Deterministic verification snapshot for exact market-data claims: the latest OHLCV row on or before the date, common technical indicators, and recent closes. Call this BEFORE making exact claims about price levels, Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD, moving averages, support/resistance or historical comparisons, and treat it as the source of truth — if another tool's output conflicts, flag the discrepancy rather than inventing a reconciled number. Keyless, reads only.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-verified-snapshot.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-verified-snapshot.mjs
  - name: get_fundamentals
    description: |
      Comprehensive fundamental picture for a company: profile, valuation multiples, margins, returns, growth, dividend — computed figures grouped by the question they answer. Absent figures are named as not covered: read absence as unknown, never as zero or as healthy. Honors the run's data_vendor choice (yahoo keyless default / alpha_vantage with key). Reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-fundamentals.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-fundamentals.mjs
  - name: get_balance_sheet
    description: |
      Balance-sheet statement rows for a company, annual or quarterly. Honors the run's data_vendor choice. Reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-balance-sheet.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-balance-sheet.mjs
  - name: get_cashflow
    description: |
      Cash-flow statement rows for a company, annual or quarterly. Honors the run's data_vendor choice. Reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-cashflow.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-cashflow.mjs
  - name: get_income_statement
    description: |
      Income-statement rows for a company, annual or quarterly. Honors the run's data_vendor choice. Reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-income-statement.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-income-statement.mjs
  - name: get_news
    description: |
      News items for one ticker over a date range: dated headlines with source, ranked by relevance. The dates are the point — match them against price moves. Honors the run's data_vendor choice (the alpha_vantage side adds the vendor's own per-item sentiment). Reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-news.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-news.mjs
  - name: get_global_news
    description: |
      Broader macroeconomic headlines over a look-back window, gathered across the standing macro queries (central banks, earnings/GDP, geopolitics, commodities). Honors the run's data_vendor choice. Reads only, cached per day.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-global-news.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-global-news.mjs
  - name: get_macro_indicators
    description: |
      A macroeconomic time series from FRED: policy rates, Treasury yields, inflation, labor, growth. Accepts friendly aliases ('cpi', 'core_pce', 'unemployment', 'fed_funds_rate', '10y_treasury', 'yield_curve', 'real_gdp', 'vix') or a raw FRED series id. Returns the series title, units, latest value, change over the window, and a recent observation table. Requires FRED_API_KEY — without it, answers DATA_UNAVAILABLE with the remedy; record that as a gap. Reads only.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-macro-indicators.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-macro-indicators.mjs
  - name: get_prediction_markets
    description: |
      Live market-implied probabilities for forward-looking events from Polymarket: Fed decisions, recession, elections, geopolitics. Returns the most-traded open markets matching the topic, each with implied probability, traded volume, resolution date and recent move. Keyless, reads only.
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/get-prediction-markets.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/get-prediction-markets.mjs
  - name: sentiment_sources
    description: |
      The sentiment analyst's complete sensory surface, in one call: (1) news headlines for the ticker, past 7 days (institutional framing); (2) StockTwits messages indexed by cashtag, each with its user-labeled Bullish/Bearish tag (fast retail signal); (3) Reddit posts from r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing with upvote and comment counts (community attention). Each source degrades gracefully: when one is unavailable its block says so explicitly — report that as reduced confidence, never fill the gap from memory. Keyless, reads only, cached per (ticker, day).
    command: node .riglane/workflows/templates/community/market-thesis-review/tools/sentiment-sources.mjs
    interpreter: node
    references:
      - tools/sentiment-sources.mjs
